answer: Each seat runs a cheap VLF lightning receiver and files GPS-timed sferic arrival times within 2 s, before the public strike map posts. The network triangulates each strike and checks every seat's times against its declared site to about 5 us; an atlas of those fits exposes co-sited keys as identical timing and merges them. One storm near a desert oasis or over the lotus ponds of Hue tests seats 1,000 km apart. Each fake needs its own ~$150 kit and a distinct site 20+ km away, so N fakes cost N real stations; replayed map data arrives too late.
